DON'T copy-paste <head> (or nav/footer) across pages. Factor shared chrome into static/partials/ and pull it in with <include src="partials/head.html" /> - one source of truth, edit once.
HTML stack: <include> is expanded server-side for every served page, resolved relative to static/ (so src="partials/head.html" → static/partials/head.html). Self-closing tag: <include src="..." />.
Keep page-specific bits (like <title>) in the page itself, AFTER the include: <head><include src="partials/head.html" /><title>This page</title></head>.
The path is contained to static/ - `..` traversal is rejected, and a symlink may point only inside static/. No-op when a page has no <include> tags.

Only the exact shape <include src="partials/x.html" /> expands (self-closing, src in double quotes, no other attributes). Push and `benmore check` refuse another shape (no `/>`, single quotes, an extra attribute: the server leaves those in the page unexpanded), a src outside the page's directory, and a target that does not exist (the page would show visitors `Include error: ... not found`). A page under static/ finds partials/x.html in the app's root partials/ first, then static/partials/x.html. A batch that defers its reload (deploy, a multi-file push) may write the page before its partial: the answer's `check` reports the missing partial until it arrives. delete_file refuses a partial a page still includes. Root pages (mustache), layouts/ and partials/kit.html are checked the same way, relative to the app directory; an included partial's own <include> tags are not expanded.

Multi-page TSX pattern: each route is a thin route.html shell (shared via <include>) that loads its own <script type=module src=/static/route.js> compiled from route.tsx. Lets a big app code-split per route AND share chrome.

gotmpl (engine: gotmpl) pages use Go html/template named templates instead (partials/*.html as {{template "name" .}}); a frontmatter `layout:` still wraps them in a mustache layout (ssr_mustache_escaping). This entry is the HTML/TSX stack.

gotmpl helpers: Sprig's process-environment `env`/`expandenv`, `getHostByName` and the key/certificate generators (genPrivateKey, genCA, genSelfSignedCert, genSignedCert and their *WithKey forms, buildCustomCert) are not available; `env` is the framework's per-app env lookup. until/untilStep/seq stop at 100,000 elements, repeat/replace/indent/join/regexReplaceAll/rand* at 4 MiB per call, and a rendered page at 64 MiB. Write-time checks execute the page with a step budget, so a template that loops without bound is refused at save.
